finding.question: why did one position block the remaining eleven scans
finding.answer: DRIVER DEFECT, not a system property. The exit came due at 2026-09-11T13:45:23.096973Z, ONE SECOND after scan 2 (2026-09-11T13:45:22.389474Z), and its window closed at 2026-09-11T13:47:23.096973Z. scripts/loop_demonstration.py ran all 12 scans first and only then attempted exits, so no housekeeping ran between scans. apex/options_pilot/entrypoint.run_pilot performs S.resume + S.attempt_exits at the start of every cycle after the first (entrypoint.py:167-172); the driver omitted that step.
finding.second_defect: the driver also REWOUND the clock: it processed scans through 16:15:24Z and then set the clock back to 2026-09-11T13:45:23.096973Z to run the exit, violating the frozen contract's own chronological discipline (LOOP_EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md 6).
consequences: scan 2 at 13:45:22 was refused BEFORE the exit was due (1.1 s early) - that refusal is correct
scans 3-12 were refused only because the position was never valued; with housekeeping the exit was due and would have been attempted
the claim 'the kernel permits at most one position at a time' is WITHDRAWN - it was never tested
the claim 'the same-underlying cap binds on real data' stands only for scan 2; scans 3-12 are driver artifacts
not_evidence_of: an unreleased reservation (the reservation is derived from the open fill, and the fill was genuinely open)
an unresolved exit (the exit RESOLVED on attempt 1 when it was finally attempted)
finding.status: DRIVER DEFECT CONFIRMED; the demonstration's refusal counts for scans 3-12 are void as evidence about the system
